inputs.original_text: A jury in Wisconsin has found a man guilty of election fraud and identity theft for requesting the ballots of Republican state Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. A Racine County jury on Tuesday found Harry Wait guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge following a two-day trial. He was acquitted of a second count of identity theft. Wait leads a group that makes false election claims. He admitted in 2022 that he requested the ballots to try to prove that the state’s voter registration system is vulnerable to fraud.
inputs.modified_text: Harry Wait was rightly found guilty for seeking ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without their consent. That matters: election rules protect voters’ autonomy and public trust. But election security cannot become a pretext for narrowing access or silencing legitimate scrutiny. Officials should investigate real vulnerabilities while ensuring reforms don’t burden the people already most likely to face barriers to voting. Accountability has to mean both enforcing the rules and making the system fairer for everyone.
